saints.name: St. Bridget of Sweden
saints.title: Religious and Co-Patroness of Europe
saints.shortBlurb: A Swedish noblewoman, wife, mother, and mystic whose Revelations stirred the Church of her age…
biography: Born about 1303 into a noble Swedish family, Bridget married young and bore eight children, among them St. Catherine of Sweden, while serving for a time at the royal court. After her husband's death she gave herself wholly to God, receiving the mystical visions later gathered as her Revelations and founding the Order of the Most Holy Saviour, the Bridgettines.

She spent her last decades at Rome, laboring for the reform of the Church and the return of the popes from Avignon, and made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land near the end of her life. She died at Rome in 1373, was canonized in 1391, and was named a co-patroness of Europe in 1999.
saints.knownFor: Her Revelations, the Bridgettine order, and reform of the Church.
